newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks were in need of correction - Cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks were in need of correction - Cenbank.

text.p: Brazilian shares were overpriced and investors used the currency woes of Asian nations as a pretext for correction on Tuesday, the president of the Central Bank Gustavo Loyola said.
"The Brazilian bolsa was in my view, expensive," Loyola told reporters at a news conference.
"The problems in Asia simply presented a very convenient pretext for some profit-taking."
Loyola said there was a causal relationship between recent devaluations in Asia and market nervousness in Brazil.
"But it has nothing to do with the economic performance of Brazil and other countries in Latin America," he said.

Loyola and the Central Bank's director of Monetary Policy Francisco "Chico" Lopes, rejected any possibility of a change in Brazilian foreign exchange and monetary policy and said they were convinced the Central Bank had the government's full support.
"Our position is very secure. Our fundamentals are very good," said Lopes, noting that Brazil's foreign reserves had recovered to $59.28 billion by July 14 after falling $1.7 billion last month.
"The Central Bank regrets the actions of the speculators. The Central Bank regrets the currency crisis in Asia. But the Central Bank remains absolutely calm," Lopes said.
"There is no reason to imagine why a speculative attack would be successful. Only a madman could think in a speculative attack against the Central Bank of Brazil would be successful," he said.
Loyola and Lopes reiteraterd government assurances that the current account gap, expected to expand to 4.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product by the end of the year, was "perfectly financiable."

Loyola also pointed out that market jitters in Brazil Tuesday were mainly limited to the stock market. He said pressure on futures and foreign exchange contracts and futures interest rate contracts was "negligble."
"The markets were nervous. The Central Bank didn't get nervous. We think we have a solid position and we are certain we have total support of the government," Loyola said.
